flags: A subsidiary of Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. entered into a purchase agreement and acquired a 60% controlling interest in White Desert Ltd, PNR Airways Ltd and Echo Charlie Ltd for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $61 million plus approximately $6 million for cash on the balance sheet.
Lindblad used $19.8 million to acquire an additional 5.0% ownership of Natural Habitat and an additional 9.9% ownership of Classic Journeys.
Lindblad forced the conversion of all 62,000 outstanding shares of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock into 9.0 million shares of common stock.

business_model.claim: Lindblad sells marine expedition cruises and land-based adventure travel experiences globally.
quotes: We provide expedition cruising and land-based adventure travel fostering a spirit of exploration and discovery, using itineraries featuring up-close encounters with wildlife and nature, history and culture, and promote guest empowerment, human connections and interactivity.

business_model.claim: The company targets individuals and families, with affluent U.S. travelers aged 50 years or older forming its largest customer demographic.
quotes: Our offerings appeal to a wide range of travelers, both individuals and families, with affluent individuals in the U.S. aged 50 years or older representing our largest demographic category.

business_model.claim: Lindblad operates through the Lindblad segment for its marine expedition brand and the Land Experiences segment covering Natural Habitat, Off the Beaten Path, DuVine, Classic Journeys, Thomson Group, White Desert, and Echo Charlie.
quotes: We operate two segments consisting of (i) the Lindblad segment, which consists of the operations of our Lindblad brand, and (ii) the Land Experiences segment, consisting of our Natural Habitat, Off the Beaten Path, DuVine, Classic Journeys brands, the Thomson Group, White Desert and Echo Charlie.

business_model.claim: The Lindblad segment operates 10 owned expedition ships and 10 seasonal charter vessels, using charters to expand travel options and test demand in new regions and seasons.
quotes: We currently operate a fleet of 10 owned expedition ships, as the National Geographic Sea Bird and the National Geographic Sea Lion completed their final expeditions this October after 16 years of service in our fleet, and 10 seasonal charter vessels (with several other vessels contracted for future expeditions) under the Lindblad brand.

We use our charter inventory as a mechanism to both increase travel options for our existing and prospective guests and also to test demand for certain areas and seasons to understand the potential for longer term deployments and additional vessel needs.

business_model.claim: Under a Brand License Agreement extending through 2040, Lindblad's owned ships carry the National Geographic name and National Geographic co-markets and sells expeditions through its internal travel division.
quotes: This relationship, which extends through 2040, includes a co-selling, co-marketing and global branding arrangement whereby our owned vessels carry the National Geographic name, and National Geographic sells our expeditions through its internal travel division.
The National Geographic agreement also serves as a significant resource for bookings for our expedition sailing business.

business_model.claim: Within Land Experiences, Natural Habitat partners with WWF through December 2028 to market conservation travel to WWF members using the WWF name and logo in return for a royalty fee.
quotes: Natural Habitat partners with WWF to offer conservation travel through a license agreement that allows Natural Habitat to use the WWF name and logo in return for a royalty fee, through December 2028.

This partnership allows Natural Habitat to promote their unique style of conservation travel to WWF’s substantial list of members and collaborate with WWF’s top scientists in training the company's guides and field team.

business_model.claim: Tour revenues consist of guest ticket revenues plus other tour revenues from pre- or post-expedition excursions, hotels, air transport, onboard goods and services, trip insurance, and cancellation fees.
quotes: Guest ticket revenues recognized from the sale of guest tickets; and

Other tour revenues from the sale of pre- or post-expedition excursions, hotel accommodations, air transportation to and from the ships and excursions, goods and services rendered onboard that are not included in guest ticket prices, trip insurance, and cancellation fees.

business_model.claim: The Lindblad segment generates the larger share of tour revenues at $435,084 (table in thousands) versus 241,327 (table in thousands) for Land Experiences, whereas Land Experiences produced higher operating income at 38,136 (table in thousands) versus $32,184 (table in thousands) for Lindblad.
Lindblad segment revenue moves with available guest nights, occupancy rates, and premium pricing reflected in net yield per available guest night, reaching 91% occupancy and $1,398 net yield.
quotes: The quality of our offerings has enabled us to achieve and maintain premium pricing in the market instead of pursuing the type of discounting offered by most cruise lines that are focused on the broader market.

Lindblad segment tour revenues of $153.4 million increased $15.8 million, or 11%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in occupancy to 91% on a 4% increase in available guest nights, driving a 6% increase in net yield to $1,398.

business_model.claim: Land Experiences revenue is driven by guest volume, the number of departures operated, pricing, trip and itinerary mix, and acquisitions.
quotes: Of the $54.0 million increase, $39.0 million is due to a 16% increase in guests traveled, and $15.0 million is related to a 7% increase in average revenue per guest, which is a combination of pricing and changes to trip and tour itinerary mixes.
Land Experiences tour revenues of $115.8 million increased $13.2 million, or 13%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in guests and operating additional trips.

Drydocking impacts operating results by reducing tour revenues and increasing cost of tours.

competitive_position.claim: Lindblad operates 10 owned expedition ships and 10 seasonal charter vessels designed to reach remote destinations inaccessible to larger cruise ships.
quotes: The small size of our vessels allows them to reach places inaccessible to larger ships.

We currently operate a fleet of 10 owned expedition ships, as the National Geographic Sea Bird and the National Geographic Sea Lion completed their final expeditions this October after 16 years of service in our fleet, and 10 seasonal charter vessels (with several other vessels contracted for future expeditions) under the Lindblad brand.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P4
competitive_position.claim: Lindblad holds a co-selling, co-marketing, and global branding partnership with National Geographic dating to 2004 and extended through 2040.
quotes: We have a longstanding relationship with the National Geographic Society, which began in 2004, and was founded on a shared interest in exploration, research, technology and conservation.

This relationship, which extends through 2040, includes a co-selling, co-marketing and global branding arrangement whereby our owned vessels carry the National Geographic name, and National Geographic sells our expeditions through its internal travel division.

competitive_position.claim: Natural Habitat serves as the exclusive conservation travel partner of World Wildlife Fund under a license agreement through December 2028.
quotes: Their dedication to environmental stewardship and exceptional travel experiences has earned them the distinction of being the exclusive conservation travel partner of World Wildlife Fund (“WWF”).
Natural Habitat partners with WWF to offer conservation travel through a license agreement that allows Natural Habitat to use the WWF name and logo in return for a royalty fee, through December 2028.

competitive_position.claim: Lindblad targets affluent U.S. travelers aged 50 years or older and maintains premium pricing rather than broad-market discounting, supported by its brand heritage since 1979 and 2025 industry awards.
quotes: Our offerings appeal to a wide range of travelers, both individuals and families, with affluent individuals in the U.S. aged 50 years or older representing our largest demographic category.

The quality of our offerings has enabled us to achieve and maintain premium pricing in the market instead of pursuing the type of discounting offered by most cruise lines that are focused on the broader market.
Lindblad has been providing marine expedition adventures and active travel experiences globally to its guests since 1979.

competitive_position.claim: In the Lindblad segment, annual occupancy rose from 77% in 2023 to 78% in 2024 and 88% in 2025, and reached 91% in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as net yield per available guest night increased 6% to $1,398.
quotes: Net yield per available guest night increased 14% to $1,335, from $1,170 in 2024, reflecting higher pricing and a ten-percentage point increase in occupancy compared with 2024.

Lindblad segment tour revenues of $153.4 million increased $15.8 million, or 11%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in occupancy to 91% on a 4% increase in available guest nights, driving a 6% increase in net yield to $1,398.
We also delivered outstanding financial results with record Adjusted EBITDA and occupancy above 90% for the third consecutive quarter.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P4 and P7; counter risks stated in P2
competitive_position.claim: Lindblad expanded its Land Experiences segment by acquiring a 60% controlling interest in White Desert and Echo Charlie during September 2026 for approximately $66.6 million in cash.
quotes: During September 2026, we acquired a 60% controlling interest in White Desert and Echo Charlie for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $66.6 million, subject to customary adjustments for working capital, cash and indebtedness.
The acquisition expands our experiential travel platform through the addition of Antarctic expedition and aviation-based travel offerings.

competitive_position.basis: stated in F1, F2, P3, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Consolidated tour revenues grew 20% to $771.0 million in 2025 and 15% to $676,411 (table in thousands) in the 9 months ended September 30, 2026, while unearned passenger revenues reached $431,788 (table in thousands) at September 30, 2026.
quotes: Tour revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $126.3 million, or 20%, to $771.0 million, compared to $644.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The increase primarily reflects $111.3 million of net cash provided by operating activities, due to increased bookings for future travel, which was partially offset by $54.6 million of cash used, net of cash acquired, to acquire a majority ownership interest in White Desert and Echo Charlie, $18.8 million of cash used in purchasing property and equipment and $19.8 million used to acquire an additional 5.0% ownership of Natural Habitat and an additional 9.9% ownership of Classic Journeys.

competitive_position.claim: Lindblad faces intense competition across the broader vacation market and risks pricing pressure from new expedition ships ordered or delivered for competitors.
quotes: The vacation industry in general is fiercely competitive with consumers being solicited for vacation travel from a variety of sources.
New expedition class ships have been ordered, are under construction, or have already been delivered for our competitors.

The growth in capacity from these new ships and future orders, without an increase in the cruise industry’s share of the vacation market, could depress expedition prices and impede our ability to maintain high yields.

competitive_position.claim: Early termination or material modification of the National Geographic Brand License Agreement or Natural Habitat's WWF license agreement would materially adversely affect Lindblad's business.
quotes: We have a Brand License Agreement with National Geographic through 2040, and any early termination or alterations to this agreement would likely have a material adverse effect on our business.

National Geographic has the right in certain instances to unilaterally terminate the Brand License Agreement early, including: in the event of a change of control; our failure to achieve specified growth benchmarks or capacity as of December 31, 2032; or a failure to meet product quality score benchmarks.
If Natural Habitat’s license agreement with WWF was terminated or modified in any material respect, our results of operations for the Land Experiences segment may be materially adversely affected.

competitive_position.claim: Port capacity constraints, local regulations, and anti-tourism countermeasures threaten access to ports of call and expedition destinations.
quotes: Certain ports and expedition destinations are facing a surge of tourism that, in certain cases, has fueled anti-tourism sentiments and related countermeasures to limit the volume of tourists allowed in these destinations, including proposed limits on cruise ships and cruise passengers or tourists in general.
Any limitations on the availability or feasibility of our ports of call or expedition destinations could adversely affect our results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Climate change, severe weather events, and evolving environmental regulations could degrade fragile destinations, disrupt itineraries, increase capital costs, or force early ship retirements.
quotes: Substantial changes to historical weather patterns could result in significant negative changes to the delicate regions that our expeditions venture, such as rising temperatures in the Arctic region that could accelerate the melting of the polar ice cap or changes to the historical weather patterns in delicate areas such as the Galápagos Islands that impacts its ecosystem and, therefore, potentially impact the viability of various expeditions, such as our polar bear tours.

Regulatory developments could, for example, result in increased costs and capital expenditures, the inability to operate ships that do not meet certain standards, the acceleration of the removal of less fuel-efficient ships from our fleet, restrict or limit our access to certain destinations or impact our operational autonomy.

competitive_position.claim: Economic recessions, geopolitical conflicts, contagious disease outbreaks, and safety or reputational incidents across the cruise industry threaten demand, occupancy, and pricing.
quotes: In past recessions, demand for our expeditionary travel offerings has been significantly negatively impacted, resulting in lower occupancy rates and adverse pricing.

In addition, adverse publicity from incidents at sea or in remote locations, even when not involving any of our ships or travel offerings, may discourage prospective travelers from taking an expedition-style trip.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2, P4, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Limited shipyard capacity, unscheduled drydockings, rising operating and royalty costs, and substantial capital and debt requirements threaten fleet availability, margins, and expansion.
quotes: In addition, there are a limited number of shipyards with the capability and capacity to build, modify or repair our ships and, accordingly, increased demand for available shipyard slots could impact our ability to construct, modify or repair ships when and as planned and/or result in stronger bargaining power on the part of the shipyards.
If prices continue to rise significantly in a short period of time, we may be unable to sufficiently increase fares or other fees to fully offset our increased costs.

Although we have no new builds currently in construction, we drydock vessels for repairs or modifications annually, and we have in the past and may in the future increase the size of our fleet by constructing or renovating additional vessels in the future.

growth_thesis.claim: For Lindblad segment occupancy and net yield growth to continue, discretionary travel demand must hold up against economic downturns, travel restrictions, and geopolitical or health disruptions, while industry capacity must not outpace demand.
quotes: In particular, a deterioration in global economic conditions that adversely affects discretionary income and consumer confidence may, in turn, result in decreased bookings, prices and onboard revenues for the expedition and cruise industries.

The growth in capacity from these new ships and future orders, without an increase in the cruise industry’s share of the vacation market, could depress expedition prices and impede our ability to maintain high yields.

quotes: Any such delays, cancellations of expeditions and/or unscheduled drydockings could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

quotes: On January 9, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Torcatt Enterprises Limitada, a holding company that owns and operates two vessels in the Galápagos Islands, for $16.0 million in cash.

quotes: There can be no assurance that any new markets will develop as anticipated or that we will have success in any new markets and, if we do not, we may be unable to recover our investment, which could adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations, including potentially impairing the value of our goodwill.

Acquisitions also carry inherent risks such as, among others: (i) the potential delay or failure of our efforts to successfully integrate business processes and realizing expected synergies; (ii) difficulty in aligning procedures, controls and/or policies; and (iii) future unknown liabilities and costs that may be associated with an acquisition.

quotes: Under the new agreement, the two companies have extended their industry-defining 20-year relationship, allowing the brand to reach new worldwide audiences through compelling new market opportunities and long-term, mutually beneficial growth strategies.

This partnership allows Natural Habitat to promote their unique style of conservation travel to WWF’s substantial list of members and collaborate with WWF’s top scientists in training the company's guides and field team.

Selling and marketing expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $27.7 million, or 32%, to $114.7 million, compared to $87.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher royalties associated with the National Geographic agreement and increased revenues driving higher commissions expense and increased marketing spend to support future growth.
